Algebra I · Lesson 6.6

Joint Proportion and Rates

Solve this lesson →All lessons

A quantity can depend on several others at the same time. The number of posters a print shop finishes depends on how many presses are running and on how long they run, and changing either one changes the count. The first two problems change the hours alone, then the presses and the hours together.

Problem
A print shop runs 6 presses for 4 hours and finishes 720 posters, every press printing at the same steady rate. The same 6 presses are then run for 7 hours. Enter how many posters they finish during those 7 hours.
Show a hint
  • Only the hours changed, since the press count stays at 6. That makes the poster count directly proportional to the hours, the direct proportion from 6.5.
  • The hours go from 4 to 7, so they are multiplied by 7447​, and the poster count is multiplied by that same factor.
Show the full solution
Multiplying the hours by 7447​ multiplies the posters by 7447​, so the shop finishes 720×74=1260720×47​=1260​. Checking another way, the 6 presses together finish 720÷4=180720÷4=180 posters an hour, and 180×7=1260180×7=1260.
Problem
That same shop runs every press at the same steady rate, and 6 presses finish 720 posters in 4 hours. Enter how many posters 15 presses finish in 6 hours.
Show a hint
  • Change one quantity at a time. Take the presses from 6 to 15 with the hours held at 4, then take the hours from 4 to 6.
  • The two scale factors are 156615​ and 6446​. Multiply 720720 by the first, then multiply that result by the second.
Show the full solution
Multiplying 720720 by 156615​ for the presses gives 18001800, and multiplying 18001800 by 6446​ for the hours gives 27002700​. The hour factor multiplies the 18001800 and not the original 720720, so the two factors multiply rather than add. Applying each one to 720720 on its own and adding gives 1800+1080=28801800+1080=2880, which is wrong.
Key idea
Joint proportion. xx is jointly proportional to yy and zz when it is directly proportional to yy with zz held fixed, and directly proportional to zz with yy held fixed. Holding zz fixed gives x=cyx=cy, and holding yy fixed makes that cc a fixed multiple of zz, so x=kyzx=kyz for one constant kk. Changing both multiplies xx by the product of the two factors. When xx is also inversely proportional to a fourth quantity ww, hold yy and zz fixed and 6.5 gives xwxw constant, so ww joins below the bar and the statement is x=kyzwx=wkyz​.
Problem
A camp's food store lasts a number of days proportional to the mass of food and inversely proportional to the number of campers. 240 kg feeds 15 campers for 32 days. Enter how many days 360 kg of food feeds 20 campers.
Show a hint
  • More food makes the store last longer and more campers make it run out sooner, so one change raises the number of days and the other lowers it.
  • The mass is multiplied by 360240240360​ and the number of campers by 20151520​, so the 32 days are multiplied by the first of those and divided by the second.
Show the full solution
Here d=kmnd=nkm​, so the first case has k=32×15240=2k=24032×15​=2 and then d=2×36020=36d=202×360​=36​. Scaling gives the same number, since with 3223​ times as much food and 4334​ times as many campers the count is 32×32×34=3632×23​×43​=36 days.
Problem
A solar array's daily output ww, in kilowatt-hours, is proportional to the number of panels pp and to the hours of sun hh, so w=kphw=kph. An array of 12 panels produces 90 kilowatt-hours in 5 hours of sun. Find kk first, then enter the output of 20 panels in 7 hours of sun, in kilowatt-hours.
Show a hint
  • One complete set of values is p=12p=12, h=5h=5 and w=90w=90, and putting all three into w=kphw=kph leaves kk as the only unknown.
  • With kk known, put p=20p=20 and h=7h=7 into the same equation and multiply.
Show the full solution
From 90=k×12×590=k×12×5 the constant is k=32k=23​, so the output of 20 panels in 7 hours is 32×20×7=21023​×20×7=210​. Skipping kk works too, since scaling by 20121220​ for panels and 7557​ for hours gives 90×2012×75=21090×1220​×57​=210.
Key idea
Group the varying quantities on one side. Dividing x=kyzx=kyz by yzyz leaves xyz=kyzx​=k, and dividing x=kyzwx=wkyz​ by yzyz and multiplying by ww leaves xwyz=kyzxw​=k. Nothing on the right side changes, so the combination on the left has the same value at every set of values. For two sets, x1y1z1=x2y2z2y1​z1​x1​​=y2​z2​x2​​, and a question about the second set is answered without ever computing kk. Every quantity xx is proportional to is written below the bar in that combination, and every quantity it is inversely proportional to above it.

A speed is a distance per unit of time, so a distance is a rate multiplied by a time. That is d=rtd=rt, used directly in Prealgebra 7.3. At one steady speed the distance is proportional to the time, and over one fixed stretch of time it is proportional to the speed. The next two problems each leave one of the three quantities unknown.

Problem
A tram holds a steady 45 kilometers per hour for 40 minutes, then a steady 66 kilometers per hour for 30 minutes. Use 1 h=60 min1 h=60 min. Enter the total distance covered, in kilometers.
Show a hint
  • Each stretch has its own rate and its own time, so d=rtd=rt applies to each one separately and the two distances add.
  • The rates are per hour, so the times have to be in hours. 40 minutes is 2332​ of an hour and 30 minutes is 1221​.
Show the full solution
The first stretch covers 45×23=3045×32​=30 km and the second covers 66×12=3366×21​=33 km, so the total in kilometers is 6363​. Leaving the times in minutes gives 45×4045×40, which is a distance in kilometer-minutes per hour and not in kilometers.
Problem
A delivery route is 288 km long. A truck covers the first 120 km at a steady 40 kilometers per hour, then covers the rest at one steady speed, and the whole route takes 6 hours. Enter the truck's speed on the second part, in kilometers per hour.
Show a hint
  • The first part has both a distance and a rate, so its time is fixed before anything about the second part is known.
  • The first part takes 3 hours, which leaves 3 of the 6 hours for the remaining 168 km.
Show the full solution
The first part takes 12040=340120​=3 hours, leaving 288−120=168288−120=168 km for the remaining 6−3=36−3=3 hours, so the second speed in kilometers per hour is 5656​. Dividing the whole route by the whole time gives 2886=486288​=48, which is the trip's overall speed and not either part's.
Key idea
d=rtd=rt is a joint relationship. Distance is proportional to the rate and to the time at once, and the constant is 11 when the units agree, so d=rtd=rt is x=kyzx=kyz with k=1k=1. Grouping the varying quantities leaves drt=1rtd​=1, and rearranging that same relationship gives r=dtr=td​ and t=drt=rd​. All three are one relationship written three ways, so knowing any two of the three quantities is enough to find the third.

Count a whole job as 11. Someone working at a steady pace who finishes in nn hours does the same amount in each of those hours, and nn of those equal amounts make the whole job, so the work done in one hour is 1nn1​ of it. That fraction per hour is a rate, and work done is the rate times the time, the same shape as d=rtd=rt.

Problem
A tiler lays a floor in 20 hours of steady work, laying the same amount in every hour. Enter the fraction of the floor laid in the first 9 hours, in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • Call the whole floor 11, so the work done in all 20 hours totals 11.
  • A steady pace means equal work in equal hours, so the tiler lays 120201​ of the floor in one hour.
Show the full solution
In one hour the tiler lays 120201​ of the floor, so nine hours of work amount to 9×120=9209×201​=209​​. The per-hour fraction is the rate, and rate times time is the amount of the job done, the same shape as d=rtd=rt with the job standing in for the distance.
Fun fact
Kepler published his third law in 1619. The square of a planet's orbital period is proportional to the cube of its mean distance from the sun, and one constant fit every planet known at the time.
Problem
One crew repaves a road in 10 hours and a second crew repaves the same road in 15 hours, each at its own steady pace. Both crews work on the road at the same time. Enter how many hours the two crews working together take to repave the road.
Show a hint
  • In one hour the first crew repaves 110101​ of the road and the second repaves 115151​, and both amounts are done during that same hour.
  • Add those two fractions over a common denominator to get the part of the road done in one hour, then the number of hours for one whole road is the reciprocal of that part.
Show the full solution
In one hour the crews repave 110+115=16101​+151​=61​ of the road, so the number of hours for one whole road is 66​. Adding the times gives 25 and averaging them gives 12.5, and both are longer than one crew takes alone, which cannot happen when a second crew helps.
Key idea
Rates add, times do not. A worker who finishes a job alone in aa hours does 1aa1​ of it in an hour, and one who finishes in bb hours does 1bb1​. Both amounts are done during the same hour, so together they do 1a+1b=a+baba1​+b1​=aba+b​ per hour, and the whole job takes the reciprocal of that, aba+ba+bab​ hours. That is smaller than both aa and bb, which is the check to run, since adding the two times or averaging them gives a time longer than the faster worker takes alone.

When two objects move along the same line at the same time, the quantity to work with is how much the distance between them changes in one hour, not either speed on its own. That change is built from both speeds, and the way to build it depends on whether the two move toward each other or one follows the other.

Problem
Two ferries leave opposite ends of a 174 km channel at the same moment and travel toward each other, one at 24 kilometers per hour and the other at 34 kilometers per hour. Enter how many kilometers the faster ferry has covered when they meet.
Show a hint
  • What settles the meeting time is how fast the distance between the two ferries shrinks, not either speed on its own. In one hour the first covers 24 km of the channel and the second covers 34 km of it.
  • The 174 km gap therefore shrinks by 58 km each hour. Dividing gives the hours until they meet, and d=rtd=rt on the faster ferry alone finishes it.
Show the full solution
The gap shrinks by 24+34=5824+34=58 km each hour, so the ferries meet after 17458=358174​=3 hours and the faster one has covered 34×3=10234×3=102​. The slower ferry covers 24×3=7224×3=72 km, and 102+72=174102+72=174 accounts for the whole channel.
Problem
A barge passes a lock at a steady 8 kilometers per hour. Three hours later a patrol boat leaves that lock along the same route in the same direction at a steady 20 kilometers per hour. Enter how far from the lock, in kilometers, the patrol boat catches the barge.
Show a hint
  • The patrol boat starts at the lock and the barge does not. Work out how far along the route the barge already is at the moment the patrol boat leaves.
  • Each hour the patrol boat covers 20 km and the barge covers 8 km, so after each hour the 24 km head start is 12 km smaller.
Show the full solution
The barge is 8×3=248×3=24 km ahead when the patrol boat starts and the gap is 20−8=1220−8=12 km smaller after each hour, so the catch takes 2412=21224​=2 hours and the distance from the lock in kilometers is 20×2=4020×2=40​. The barge has then been moving 5 hours, and 8×5=408×5=40 agrees.
Key idea
Closing rate. Two objects moving toward each other each remove their own distance from the gap during the same hour, so the gap shrinks at r1+r2r1​+r2​ per hour. When one follows the other, both move the same way, so in one hour the one behind gains r1r1​ while the one in front moves r2r2​ further away, and the gap shrinks by only the difference r1−r2r1​−r2​. The catch happens only when r1r1​ is the larger. Either way the gap closes at a steady rate, so d=rtd=rt applies to the gap itself with the closing rate as rr. A head start stated in time is turned into a head start in distance the same way.

Every relationship in this chapter was one combination staying fixed while its parts changed. 6.1 fixed abba​, 6.2 multiplied by a fraction worth 11, 6.3 and 6.4 fixed the second part of a comparison at 100, and 6.5 fixed yxxy​ or xyxy. The combination fixed here is longer, and the last two problems use it.

Problem
The number of bricks a crew lays is proportional to the number of masons and to the number of days worked. Eight masons lay 2016 bricks in 6 days. A contractor needs 3780 bricks laid in 5 days. Enter how many masons that takes.
Show a hint
  • Write bb for bricks, mm for masons and dd for days. Joint proportion means bmdmdb​ has the same value for both jobs, and here the unknown is in the denominator.
  • Eight masons working 6 days is 48 mason-days for 2016 bricks. Find the bricks one mason lays in one day, then ask how many masons put 3780 bricks into 5 days.
Show the full solution
With bb bricks, mm masons and dd days, joint proportion gives bmd=kmdb​=k, and from the first job k=20168×6=42k=8×62016​=42 bricks per mason per day. Then 3780=42×m×53780=42×m×5, so the number of masons is 1818​. Scaling works without kk too. The bricks are multiplied by 158815​ and the days by 5665​, so the masons are multiplied by 158÷56=94815​÷65​=49​, and 8×94=188×49​=18.
Problem
A workshop's looms are identical and each one weaves at the same steady rate. Six of them weaving for 5 hours produce 210 meters of cloth. Four of them are set to produce 252 meters of the same cloth. Enter the number of hours that takes.
Show a hint
  • How much cloth comes off depends on both how many looms run and how long they run, so work out first how many meters one loom weaves in one hour.
  • Six looms for 5 hours is 30 loom-hours of weaving in all, so 210÷30210÷30 gives the meters per loom-hour. Four looms running together weave four times that much each hour.
Show the full solution
Six looms for 5 hours is 30 loom-hours, and 210÷30=7210÷30=7 meters per loom-hour. Four looms weave 4×7=284×7=28 meters each hour, so the number of hours is 252÷28=9252÷28=9​. The cloth produced is jointly proportional to the number of looms and to the number of hours, so the single rate of 7 meters per loom-hour accounts for both changes at once.

Every relationship in this lesson had one constant and several quantities that change, and the work was always to gather the changing ones on one side of the bar and read the constant off the other. Distance, work rate and closing rate all have that shape. That closes chapter 6. Chapter 7, Graphing Lines, opens with 7.1, The Cartesian Plane.

Practice these ideas

Practice
The mass of a metal plate is proportional to its length and to its width. A plate 4 cm long and 9 cm wide has a mass of 54 grams. Enter the mass, in grams, of a plate 4 cm long and 14 cm wide.
Show the solution
Only the width changed, by a factor of 149914​, so the mass in grams is 54×149=8454×914​=84​. Nine divides 54 exactly six times, so the product reduces to 6×146×14.
Practice
WW is jointly proportional to uu and vv, so W=kuvW=kuv for one constant kk. When u=6u=6 and v=4v=4, W=264W=264. Enter the value of kk.
Show the solution
Substituting gives 264=24k264=24k, so k=26424=11k=24264​=11​. Checking it back, 11×6×4=26411×6×4=264.
Practice
A worker's pay is proportional to the number of shifts worked and to the hours in each shift. Four shifts of 6 hours pay 528 dollars in total. Enter the pay in dollars for 5 shifts of 9 hours.
Show the solution
The constant is 5284×6=224×6528​=22 dollars per hour, so the pay for 5 shifts of 9 hours is 22×5×9=99022×5×9=990​. Since 55 shifts is 5445​ of 44 and 99 hours is 9669​ of 66, the pay is also 528×54×96528×45​×69​, which is 990990 again.
Practice
PP is jointly proportional to qq and rr, and P=189P=189 when q=3q=3 and r=9r=9. Enter PP when q=5q=5 and r=4r=4.
Show the solution
The constant is k=18927=7k=27189​=7, so P=7×5×4=140P=7×5×4=140​. Scaling agrees, since 189×53×49=140189×35​×94​=140.
Practice
yy is directly proportional to mm and inversely proportional to nn. When m=8m=8 and n=6n=6, y=24y=24. Enter yy when m=15m=15 and n=10n=10.
Show the solution
Grouping gives ynm=k=24×68=18myn​=k=824×6​=18, so y=18×1510=27y=1018×15​=27​. Scaling agrees, since 24×158×35=2724×815​×53​=27.
Practice
The number of days a water store lasts is proportional to the volume stored and inversely proportional to the number of households drawing on it. 900 liters lasts 12 households 15 days. Enter the number of days 1200 liters lasts 20 households.
Show the solution
Substituting the first store's numbers into d=kVHd=HkV​ gives k=15×12900=15k=90015×12​=51​, and then d=15⋅120020=12d=51​⋅201200​=12​. The households grew by the larger factor, 5335​ against 4334​ for the volume, so the number of days is below 15.
Practice
A tram covers 78 km in 65 minutes at a steady speed. Enter how many kilometers it covers in 100 minutes at that same speed.
Show the solution
The tram covers 7865=1.26578​=1.2 km each minute, so in 100 minutes it covers 1.2×100=1201.2×100=120​. Scaling the distance by the same factor as the time lands on the same number, since 78×10065=12078×65100​=120.
Practice
A survey drone covers 189 km in 3 hours 30 minutes at a steady speed. Use 1 h=60 min1 h=60 min. Enter the drone's speed in kilometers per hour.
Show the solution
The time is 7227​ hours, so the speed in kilometers per hour is 189÷72=189×27=54189÷27​=189×72​=54​.
Practice
A painter finishes a mural in 15 hours, covering the same amount of wall in every hour. Enter the fraction of the mural that is finished once 6 hours of work are done, in lowest terms.
Show the solution
One hour covers 115151​ of the mural, so six hours cover 615156​, which reduces to 2552​​. Working at a steady rate makes the fraction finished the same as the fraction of the time spent.
Practice
One conveyor loads a barge in 14 hours and a second conveyor loads the same barge in 35 hours, each at its own steady rate. Both run at once on one barge. Enter how many hours they take to load it.
Show the solution
In one hour the conveyors load 114+135=570+270=770=110141​+351​=705​+702​=707​=101​ of the barge, so the number of hours is 1010​. Loading one tenth of the barge each hour means the whole barge takes ten hours, while adding the two times would give 49 hours, longer than either conveyor needs on its own.
Practice
Pumps A and B running together drain a tank in 12 hours, and pump A alone drains the tank in 20 hours. Enter how many hours pump B alone takes to drain the tank.
Show the solution
Pump B drains 112−120=560−360=260=130121​−201​=605​−603​=602​=301​ of the tank per hour, so the number of hours is 3030​. Checking, 120+130=112201​+301​=121​.
Practice
Two drones 245 km apart set off at the same moment and fly toward each other along the same line, one at 42 kilometers per hour and the other at 28 kilometers per hour. Enter how many kilometers the faster drone has flown when they meet.
Show the solution
The gap closes at 42+28=7042+28=70 km each hour, so they meet after 24570=7270245​=27​ hours and the faster drone has flown 42×72=14742×27​=147​. The slower drone flies 28×72=9828×27​=98 km, and 147+98=245147+98=245 accounts for the whole gap.
Practice
A hiker leaves a trailhead at a steady 7 kilometers per hour. Four hours later a cyclist leaves the same trailhead on the same path at a steady 21 kilometers per hour. Enter how far from the trailhead, in kilometers, the cyclist draws level with the hiker.
Show the solution
The hiker is 7×4=287×4=28 km ahead when the cyclist starts, and the lead shrinks by 21−7=1421−7=14 km each hour, so the catch takes 2 hours and the distance from the trailhead in kilometers is 21×2=4221×2=42​. The hiker has walked 6 hours by then, and 7×6=427×6=42 agrees.
Practice
Sprinkler C waters a field in 10 hours and sprinkler D waters the same field in 40 hours, each at its own steady rate. Both run together for 4 hours, then sprinkler C is switched off and sprinkler D finishes alone. Enter how many further hours sprinkler D needs.
Show the solution
Together they water 110+140=540=18101​+401​=405​=81​ of the field an hour, so four hours finish 48=1284​=21​ of it. Sprinkler D covers the remaining half at 140401​ an hour, needing 1/21/40=201/401/2​=20​ further hours. Adding the two solo times, or averaging them, answers a different question.
Practice
A packing plant running 8 machines for 5 hours a day takes 12 days to finish an order, every machine working at the same steady rate. The next order is twice as large and must be finished in 10 days using 12 machines. Enter how many hours a day those machines must run.
Show the solution
The first order is 8×5×12=4808×5×12=480 machine-hours, so the second is 960960, and 960÷(12×10)=8960÷(12×10)=8​. Forgetting to double the order gives 480÷120=4480÷120=4 instead.
Practice
A data hall's running cost is proportional to the number of racks and to the hours online, and inversely proportional to its efficiency rating. 20 racks online 6 hours at rating 4 cost 900 dollars. Enter the cost in dollars of 28 racks online 10 hours at rating 8.
Show the solution
Grouping gives Cerh=krhCe​=k, and the first set fixes k=900×4120=30k=120900×4​=30. Then C=30×28×108=1050C=830×28×10​=1050​.
Practice
Two cyclists ride toward each other along a 190 km road. The first sets out from one end at a steady 15 kilometers per hour. Two hours later the second sets out from the far end at a steady 25 kilometers per hour. Enter how far from the first cyclist's start, in kilometers, the two meet.
Show the solution
The first cyclist covers 15×2=3015×2=30 km before the second starts, leaving a 160 km gap, and the two then close on each other at 15+25=4015+25=40 km per hour, so they meet 4 hours after the second sets out. The first has ridden 6 hours by then, so the distance in kilometers is 15×6=9015×6=90​. The second rides 25×4=10025×4=100 km, and 90+100=19090+100=190.
